title: Describing an inequality solution
observableEvidence: Determines which values make an inequality true and explains that the solution is a set of values satisfying the statement.
prompt: For the inequality n + 2 < 7, decide whether n = 3 and n = 6 are solutions. Then describe the full solution set in words.
solutionRepresentation: n = 3 is a solution because 3 + 2 < 7. n = 6 is not because 6 + 2 is not less than 7. The solution set is all numbers less than 5.
solutionMethod: Test each candidate by substitution, then identify the boundary and describe every value that makes the inequality true.

deterministicValidator.canonicalAnswer: 3 is a solution; 6 is not; all numbers less than 5
acceptedAnswers: 3 is a solution; 6 is not; all numbers less than 5
deterministicValidator.equivalenceNotes: Accept inequality notation or equivalent words describing the complete set below 5.

hintSteps.prompt: Test each proposed value, then ask what values are on the same satisfying side of the boundary.
hintSteps.question: What value makes n + 2 equal 7, and which side of it makes the expression smaller?

review.originalityStatement: New candidate item drafted from first principles for this repository; it does not reproduce or paraphrase proprietary or contest material.

accessibilityNotes: State the inequality and candidate values in text; the solution set can be described verbally without a number-line graphic.
accessibleAlternative: Read aloud or display: For n plus two less than seven, test three and six, then say all numbers that make the statement true.
